On the evening of April 18, 1891, a railway accident took place at Kipton Crossing. The Toledo express, which was traveling at an estimated speed of 45 miles per hour and was running twenty minutes behind schedule, collided with a stationary freight train that had been shunted onto the main line.

The accident resulted in the deaths of the fireman and the express engineer, Michael O'Hara. Additionally, nine passengers were injured, though none of these injuries were fatal. The express train was composed of a locomotive, a sleeper, two coaches, and a baggage car; based on the conductor's count at Cleveland, there were 61 passengers on board. The damage to the rolling stock was valued at 14,200 dollars.

An investigating board determined that the cause of the accident was the failure of James Caldwell, the station agent at Oberlin, to deliver the order that established a meeting point at Elyria. Consequently, the board recommended that the company dismiss Caldwell and implement the block signal system across the entire division. The company carried out both of these recommendations within one year.

raw: On the evening of April 18, 1891, a railway accident took place at Kipton Crossing. The Toledo express, which was running twenty minutes late and traveling at an estimated speed of forty-five miles per hour, collided with a stationary freight train that had been moved onto the main line. The crash resulted in the deaths of the express train’s engineer, Michael O'Hara, and the fireman, while nine passengers were injured, though none of their injuries proved fatal. An investigation board determined that James Caldwell, the station agent at Oberlin, had failed to deliver the order that specified a meeting point at Elyria. The express train consisted of a locomotive, a baggage car, two coaches, and a sleeper car, and carried sixty-one passengers according to the conductor’s count at Cleveland. The damage to the rolling stock was valued at fourteen thousand two hundred dollars. The board recommended that the block signal system be introduced across the entire division and that Caldwell be dismissed, and the company carried out both of these recommendations within the year.
